question: Should OpenClaw allow scheme-level wildcards such as `chrome-extension://*` in `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins`, or should origin flexibility stay limited to exact custom-scheme origins and separately constrained pattern surfaces?
rationale: This changes the browser-origin trust boundary for Control UI/WebChat, and repository policy treats origin/config/security behavior as maintainer-owned rather than an autonomous fix shape.

options.title: Prefer constrained pattern policy
options.body: Keep the issue open only for a schema-validated, documented, audited pattern surface with negative security tests instead of ad hoc prefix matching in `allowedOrigins`.

options.title: Limit to exact origins and extension route
options.body: Close or narrow this request if maintainers want Chrome extension access handled by exact origin matching and the dedicated `/browser/extension` pairing path.

options.title: Allow scheme wildcard in existing field
options.body: Accept `chrome-extension://*` directly in `allowedOrigins`, acknowledging that all Chrome extension origins can reach the authenticated WebSocket gate.

recommendation.title: Prefer constrained pattern policy
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open only for a schema-validated, documented, audited pattern surface with negative security tests instead of ad hoc prefix matching in `allowedOrigins`.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the recent gateway/browser extension security path and most current history for the origin checker.
